Typed Objects Example

A C++ class packed into typed blocks, sent over gxStream, stored in a gxDatabase file, exported to plain text and imported back.

What It Shows

The whole life of a typed object in DataReel:

  1. The TradeEvent class packs itself into a block that starts with a small type header: a four character type code, a layout version and the body size. Any program that reads the block knows what it holds, and a later version of the class can still read old blocks. The body is written field by field with fixed sizes, so it does not depend on structure padding.
  2. A client sends each packed object over TLS with gxStream (AddBlock). A server thread in the same program stores every block in a gxDatabase file and answers with its file address.
  3. The client reads each object back by address (RequestBlock) and checks it.
  4. The program walks the database file, unpacks every object and exports it to text: one key=value line per object under a comment line that says the same thing in plain words. The text file does not depend on the binary layout, so it is the long-lived, portable form.
  5. The text is imported into a second database file and every object is compared with the original, field by field.

gxStream is only the transport: the objects are the program's own class, and the database file stores whatever bytes the class packs.

Running It

gxStream always uses TLS, so this example needs a certificate and key for localhost. A self-signed one is enough for a test (see also Certificates):

openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem \
  -days 30 -subj "/CN=localhost" -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"
typed_objects cert.pem key.pem --ca cert.pem

Use --insecure instead of --ca to skip the certificate check (testing only). It writes typed_objects.gxd, typed_objects.txt and typed_objects_import.gxd in the current folder and exits with 0 when every object survives all three steps.
